title: Durable checkpoint, interruption, replay, and crash recovery contract

durability.checkpoint: A checkpoint is complete only after its canonical payload and digest are durably recorded; a caller claim is not evidence.
durability.identity: A checkpoint is immutable and binds task revision, session, worktree, worker, lease, sequence, and state digest.
durability.restart: Restart may use only the latest verified checkpoint for the exact task/session/worktree and a strictly newer fenced lease.

idempotence.rule: A retry with the same operation ID is accepted only when its canonical operation payload and result digest are identical; it returns the original result without a second mutation.
idempotence.replay: A replay consumes a checkpoint event at most once; a duplicate event ID, checkpoint ID, or operation ID with changed content fails closed.
idempotence.ambiguity: A missing or conflicting durable result is ambiguous and enters safe_mode; it is never guessed successful or retried with changed identity.

failure_semantics.side_effects: The checker and reference model perform no network, provider, process, Git, Coordinator, AWQ, AWG, UI, or filesystem operation.

privacy.projection: Evidence contains only stable opaque identifiers, bounded integers, revisions, dispositions, and digests.

compatibility.canonical_json: UTF-8 JSON, sorted keys, compact separators, no trailing newline
compatibility.minor_change: a compatible checker and new versioned fixture are required for additions

limitations: This contract validates supplied observations and does not prove that Coordinator durably recorded them or that a host or agent actually failed.
The reference model does not implement a storage engine, fsync, process supervisor, or distributed consensus.
A passing trace does not establish provider availability, filesystem isolation, hosted CI, remote execution, or runtime recovery.
follow_up: AR-0008 defines the privacy-safe event journal and provenance chain.
AR-0018 implements production supervision and durable recovery against Coordinator contracts.
